segments.text: To manipulate the porosity of these materials, various activation and carbonization methods are employed. Chemical and physical activation techniques [ [10] , [11] , [12] , [13] ], phase separation [ 14 ], and template methods [ 15 ] have all been extensively utilized. Among these methods, the activation process followed by the carbonization process, effectively transforms carbonaceous materials into porous materials of micro, meso, and macro scales. Such materials have been extensively researched and applied in solving energy constraints due to the necessity of replacing fossil fuels with renewable sources of energy.

segments.text: The demand for high-performance electrochemical energy storage devices, exemplified by supercapacitors, necessitates attributes such as high power density, moderate energy density, and wide operating temperatures [ 11 ]. This has prompted intensive research into new materials and their energy storage mechanisms. Supercapacitors operate through electrostatic charge attraction (Electric double-layer capacitor, EDLC) [ 11 , 16 ] and redox reactions (Pseudocapacitor) [ 4 ]. While EDLC-type materials excel in power density and cycling stability, they often fall short in energy density [ 17 , 18 ]. Conversely, pseudocapacitive materials offer higher energy density but often exhibit reduced cycling stability [ 19 ]. Consequently, recent investigations focus on leveraging porous carbonaceous materials to enhance energy density, power density, and cycling stability.

segments.text: Recent studies have spotlighted bio-waste-derived FPC materials for these applications. For instance, Hwang et al. harnessed natural silk to produce highly porous carbon, boasting impressive electrochemical properties with substantial retention after cycles [ 20 ]. Similarly, coconut shells yielded highly porous carbon nanospheres with excellent cycling stability [ 21 ]. Sunflower seed shells and carrageenan were also used, displaying promising electrochemical performance [ 22 , 23 ]. Notably, attention has shifted toward phosphoric acid activation to create mesopores alongside micropores [ 22 , 24 ].

segments.text: In contrast to previous studies that have focused on other bio-waste sources, such as silk, coconut shell, and sunflower seed shells [ [20] , [21] , [22] ], this research uniquely centers on Alnus nepalensis bio-waste. By extending the scope of wood waste applications to encompass both energy storage and pollutant removal, this study aims to unveil the diverse capabilities of Alnus nepalensis -derived FPC material that was chemically activated by H 3 PO 4 . The choice of H 3 PO 4 as activating agent was due to its well-reported superiority in dehydrating the lignocellulosic material at lower temperature (75 °C). Moreover, H 3 PO 4 also helps to form a bridge that connects the fragments of biopolymers (layers of carbon structure) by forming phosphate and polyphosphate linkages. It helps in overall structural dilation, opens the pores, and enlarges the surface area of lignocellulosic material [ 25 ].

segments.text: Alnus nepalensis commonly known as the Nepalese Alder or Utis, is a prominent tree species found abundantly across the lush landscapes of Nepal [ 26 ]. This versatile tree holds great significance in various domains, particularly in the realm of carpentry, where its unique properties and characteristics make it a valuable resource. Its carpentry waste (bio-waste) has been utilized in this study.

segments.text: In summary, the present investigation delves into utilizing Alnus nepalensis bio-waste as a novel and promising precursor material for synthesizing highly functionalized porous carbonaceous materials. By exploring its distinctive properties and applications, this study aims to contribute to the expanding field of sustainable materials, energy storage, and pollutant removal, ultimately advancing both environmental and technological fronts.

segments.text: Alnus nepalensis wood waste was gathered from nearby carpentry in Lalitpur, Nepal. Alnus nepalensis , commonly called Utis in Nepal, is a significant multipurpose tree. It is found at an altitude of 900–2700 m above sea level [ 26 ]. The main products of these trees are wood, green leaves, and fuel. The leaf decay is also used as manure and to safeguard soil conservation [ 27 ].

segments.text: All chemicals used in this study were analytically graded. 85 % pure phosphoric acid having 1.73 g/mL of specific gravity was procured from Fischer Scientific, India (P) Ltd., and it was used as the activating agent to make FPC. Double-distilled water with a resistivity of 18.2 MΩ-cm was used throughout the experimental work. Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), Carbon black, and N-methyl pyroline (NMP) were procured from Sigma-Aldrich (USA). Similarly, Ni-foam was procured from PRED MATERIALS International (USA) for use as a current collector electrode. An electrochemical measurement was performed in a 6.0 M potassium hydroxide (KOH) electrolyte which was purchased from Ajax Finechem, Thermo Fisher Scientific. The Malachite green dye was acquired from the esteemed supplier Alfa Aesar (A13572), while the aqueous NH 3 (30 %) was obtained from the reputable source, Baker.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: FPC was obtained via a previously reported synthesis protocol [ 3 , 28 ]. The collected wood waste of Alnus nepalensis (Utis), was washed with tap water 3, 4 times, sun-dried for a week, pulverized using a high-speed electric wood grinder, and put through a sieve of 150 μm to obtain fine wood powder. Grinding FPC has multiple benefits. Grinding of FPC increases surface area, enhances ion transport, reduces diffusion path length, improves electrical contact, and enables better pore accessibility. These effects collectively lead to higher capacitance, faster charge-discharge rates, and improved overall performances of supercapacitors in electrochemical energy storage systems. The enhancement of the specific surface area is also crucial for the adsorption processes of pollutants like dyes [ [28] , [29] , [30] ].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: The obtained fine powder was chemically activated by soaking in 85 % H 3 PO 4 for 24 h and oven dried for 2 h at 110 °C.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: To carbonize the obtained wood powder, a tubular furnace set at a temperature of 400 °C was used under the flow of N 2 at 100 mL/min for 3 h. Then it was cooled down to room temperature and washed several times using distilled water till its pH turn out to be neutral. The functionalized porous carbon (FPC) thus obtained was finally dried at 110 °C and ground to a fine powder and was used for both physical and electrochemical analyses [ 18 , 28 ].

segments.text: The FPC-electrode-material was assembled as reported in previous studies [ 11 ]. A mixture composed of 8 mg of FPC, 1 mg carbon black powder, and 1 mg PDVF was dissolved in 200 μL NMP solution. A slurry was obtained by grinding the mixture which was coated on Ni-foam (70 μL of slurry on a 1 cm 2 area). The slurry-coated Ni foam was dried at 70 °C for 12 h. Thereafter, it was pressed at 10 kPa for a minute. The uncoated part of Ni-foam was used for connecting a copper lead wire. Thus assembled FPC-electrode was activated by immerging in 6. O M KOH solution for 12 h.

segments.text: A stock solution of MG dye was prepared with a concentration of 20 ppm by dissolving 0.020 g of the dye in 1 L of double-distilled water. The experimental set up began by placing 100 mL of the MG dye solution into 250 mL Erlenmeyer flask. Into the flask, 0.02 g of FPC was carefully introduced, and the mixture was stirred at 400 rpm for about 5 min while maintaining a neutral pH level. During the stirring process, 3 mL of the resulting mixture was sequentially transferred into individual micro-centrifuge tubes at 2 min intervals. This process was repeated five times. Afterward, to eliminate insoluble particles, centrifugation was performed on all five micro-centrifuge tubes at 400 rpm for 5 min. The supernatant liquid obtained from this step was then employed for subsequent analysis using UV–Vis spectrometer (Scinco, Mega-2100, Double Beam).

segments.text: TGA/DSC of the raw wood powder of Alnus nepalensis, as depicted in Fig. 1 , shows the completion of the carbonization process below 400 °C similar to the findings in our previous studies [ 11 , 32 ]. Only a small amount of mass was lost at temperatures close to 100 °C, which was ascribed to dehydration, according to the TG curve. A sharp apex in the DSC curve at 100 °C served as proof. Similar to this, a peak with an indistinct contraction was seen between 200 and 300 °C. Correspondingly, in the TG, a mass loss was seen in the DSC curve due to the breakdown of hemicelluloses, which was clearly seen at 300 °C. A noticeable mass loss was found in the 300–400 °C range in the TG curve after additional heating. This was also confirmed by a sharp depression at around 390 °C of the DSC curve. From the results, it was accepted that cellulose broke down and got converted into organic volatile matter at around 300 °C. From the TG curve, it is obvious that the precursor material lost about 60 % of mass at a carbonization temperature of 400 °C used in this study [ 11 , 33 ]. Above 400 °C the carbonization of the precursor became stable. Therefore, 400 °C was considered to be a suitable carbonization temperature.

segments.text: The amorphous nature of FPC is further supported by Raman spectra ( Fig. 2 b). The D band (1357 cm −1 ) signifies defects and disorder in the carbon structure, while the G band (1593 cm −1 ) represents sp 2 hybridized carbon atoms in graphitic structures. A G/D ratio of approximately 1.5 indicates a highly disordered carbon structure, favorable for ion movement and electrochemical reactions in energy storage devices [ 34 ].

segments.text: The FTIR spectra ( Fig. 2 c) reinforce the functionalization of FPC. Peaks at 3432 cm −1 are attributed to –OH stretching vibrations of carboxyl, phenol, alcohol, and absorbed water, indicating enhanced functionalization due to H 3 PO 4 impregnation [ 27 ]. The band between 2330 and 2359 cm −1 is attributed to aliphatic C–H stretching absorption [ [2] , [3] , [4] ]. Other peaks like the one at approximately 1591 cm −1 [ 25 , 36 ], indicate olefinic C <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.0" width="20.666667pt" height="16.000000pt" viewBox="0 0 20.666667 16.000000" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"><metadata> Created by potrace 1.16, written by Peter Selinger 2001-2019 </metadata><g transform="translate(1.000000,15.000000) scale(0.019444,-0.019444)" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"><path d="M0 440 l0 -40 480 0 480 0 0 40 0 40 -480 0 -480 0 0 -40z M0 280 l0 -40 480 0 480 0 0 40 0 40 -480 0 -480 0 0 -40z"/></g></svg> C vibrations in aromatic rings. The presence of broadband around 1107 cm −1 signifies C–O stretching in various functional groups, often associated with oxidized carbon. These observations collectively suggest the formation of oxygen-containing groups as a result of efficient H 3 PO 4 functionalization.

segments.text: The BET results ( Fig. 2 d) reveal FPC's porous characteristics. The N 2 adsorption-desorption isotherms, analyzed using the Brunauer-Deming-Deming-Teller (BDDT) method, show a Type II, H3 isotherm, indicating the presence of both micropores and mesopores. The sudden rise in N 2 uptake below P/P0 < 0.1 indicates a dearth of micropores, while a steady increase in nitrogen uptake up to P/P0 = 0.4 suggests the existence of mesopores. Beyond P/P0 = 0.5, a clear hysteresis loop reflects the abundance of mesopores [ [37] , [38] , [39] ]. The BET-specific surface area, pore size, and pore volume of FPC were determined and are outlined in Table 2 .

segments.text: In the capacity retention (%) analysis, the focus was on assessing the long-term cycling stability of the FPC-electrode, which is a crucial aspect of its practical application in supercapacitors. Supercapacitors are often subjected to daily charge-discharge cycles, causing gradual degradation over time [ 2 ]. One important parameter that reflects this stability is the capacity retention percentage. This percentage represents the ratio of the capacitance maintained after a certain number of cycles to the initial capacitance.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: In the present study, the FPC-electrode underwent 1000 continuous charge-discharge cycles at a fixed current density of 3 A/g ( Fig. 6 ). Remarkably, at the end of this cycling test, the FPC-electrode retained approximately 98.4 % of its initial capacitance. This high capacity retention indicates that the electrode's performance remained robust and relatively unchanged even after prolonged cycling, suggesting excellent cycling stability. Such behavior is a positive indicator for practical supercapacitor applications, where long-term reliability is essential.

segments.text: The FPC prepared in this study was also tested for its adsorption behavior. It is worth mentioning that the adsorption capacity of an adsorbent mainly depends on its surface functionality which is imparted in the material during the activation process. Other factors that contribute to adsorption capacity are the active surface area, pore size, pore volume, and morphology. On the other hand, variables like initial dye concentration, contact time, dose, and pH of the solution are important factors that affect the adsorption of dye. Therefore, by optimizing these parameters, the process of removing dye or treating wastewater can be improved.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: The spectrophotometric method was used to study the adsorption of MG dye at various alkaline pH. For this, a consistent quantity of 20 parts per million (ppm) of this dye was taken. Additionally, the dye was mixed with a standard dose of 0.030 g of FPC for every 100 mL of the solution. To evaluate the influence of pH, the pH levels of the solution were altered within the range of 8.5–12.5. Fig. 9 a illustrates the effect of pH on the adsorption of MG dye, the maximum adsorption was observed at pH 10.5 [ 24 , 47 , 48 ]. This observation indicates that there exists an optimal pH condition for maximizing the effective adsorption of the dye molecules onto the FPC surface. As the pH of the solution increases the FPC's surface acquires an augmented negative charge. This negativity emerges due to the attraction and binding of hydroxide ions (OH-) from the solution onto the surface of the FPC. Consequently, this negative surface charge becomes attractive to the positively charged MG dye molecules, facilitating their binding to the FPC [ 47 , 49 ] surface. However, an intriguing phenomenon takes place beyond the pH of 10.5. The heightened negativity of the FPC's surface starts to evoke a repulsion effect against the negatively charged MG dye molecule; as a result, there is a decrease in the percentage of dye removal from the solution. This repulsion effect can be likened to the way similar poles of magnets push each other apart. This explains the dip observed in the percentage of dye removal after pH 10.5. In all the cases, the measurement time was about 5 min assuming that the adsorption of dye would complete in this time period.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: In this research, FPC was successfully prepared by the wood waste of Alnus nepalensis through a two-step process: initial activation with H 3 PO 4 and subsequent carbonization at 400 °C. This material was then meticulously characterized for its dual applications as a supercapacitor electrode and an effective adsorbent for MG dye.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: The resulting FPC exhibited remarkable characteristics, as revealed by various analyses. BET and TEM measurements confirmed its highly porous nature, while FTIR, XRD, and Raman analysis indicated a functionalized, amorphous, and defective structure. The BET analysis yielded an active surface area of 1498 m 2 /g, a pore volume of 1.2 cm 3 /g, and a pore size of 4.6 nm.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: Electrochemical evaluation of the FPC electrode demonstrated excellent EDLC-type supercapacitive performance, boasting a specific capacitance of 156.3 F/g, an energy density of 5.1 Wh/kg, a power density of 183.6 W/kg, and an impressive retention capacity of 98.4 % after 1000 galvanostatic charge-discharge cycles.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: Furthermore, the FPC material exhibited notable adsorption capabilities, with the highest adsorption capacity observed at pH 10.5 and a dose of 0.030 g. Under these conditions, a solution containing 20 ppm of MG dye was rapidly removed, achieving a remarkable 95.6 % removal within 2 min and reaching a maximum removal efficiency of 99.6 % within 6 min.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\同体系文献补充_第二批_20261017\定向扩搜40至60篇_20261017\sources\OA052\main.xml
segments.text: In conclusion, this study demonstrates the successful modification of Alnus nepalensis wood waste into a versatile material with dual functionality. The FPC material's outstanding performance as a supercapacitor electrode material, coupled with its remarkable adsorption capacity for MG dye, positions it as a promising candidate for addressing energy storage and environmental challenges. These results open new avenues for sustainable utilization of bio-waste materials in advanced energy storage and environmental remediation applications.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The increasing demand for sustainable and efficient energy storage systems has driven extensive research efforts in the development of high-performance supercapacitors [ [ 1 ]]. These devices offer a promising alternative to traditional batteries due to their high power density, rapid charge/discharge rates, and long cycling stability [ [ 2 ]]. As the demand for supercapacitors continues to rise, there is a compelling requirement for cost-effective and eco-friendly carbon-based electrode materials.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: This study explores the potential of wood waste from Terminalia elliptica , commonly called ‘Satisal’ in Nepali, is a readily available and fast growing hardwood tree species native to Nepal and the broader South Asian region. Its abundance and rapid growth make it a promising renewable source for producing activated carbon electrodes, aligning with the pursuit of sustainable and renewable energy solutions [ [ 2 ]]. Beyond its traditional uses, Terminalia elliptica wood waste possesses inherent characteristics that make it ideal for activated carbon production. Its high cellulose content and robust structure contribute to the development of highly porous and chemically stable carbon materials, crucial for enhancing electrode performance [ [ 3 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Additionally, utilizing Terminalia elliptica as a biomass source aligns with local sustainability initiatives in Nepal and the South Asian region. This approach not only promotes the development of clean energy technologies but also empowers local communities by creating new economic opportunities through responsible waste management.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Compared to conventional biomass sources like coconut shells or bamboo, Terminalia elliptica offers advantages such as faster growth rates, wider availability, and potentially lower processing costs. Additionally, its inherent physical and chemical properties may lead to the development of unique activated carbon characteristics with superior electrochemical performance [ [ 4 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Motivation: Carbon-based materials have become the preferred choice for supercapacitor electrodes due to their excellent electrical conductivity, high surface area, and chemical stability [ [ 5 ]]. However, a significant gap remains in our understanding of how the carbonization temperature, a critical variable in material synthesis, influences the electrochemical performance of renewable carbon electrodes derived from biomass.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Recent progress: In recent years, there has been a surge of interest in biomass-derived carbon materials as a sustainable alternative to conventional carbon sources [ [ 6 ]]. Biomass resources such as agricultural waste, wood, and plant residues, offer a renewable and abundant resource for producing activated carbon (AC) electrodes. However, the carbonization process, especially the temperature at which it is carried out, has a profound influence on the physicochemical properties of the resulting ACs. These properties, such as surface area, porosity, and heteroatom content, are crucial in determining the electrochemical performance of these AC electrodes [ [ 7 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Research objectives: This study aims to bridge this knowledge gap by systematically exploring the relationship between carbonization temperatures and the electrochemical properties of biomass-derived carbon electrodes. The principal research objective is to elucidate how distinct thermal conditions impact the structural characteristics and electrochemical behavior of resulting carbon materials. Furthermore, we aim to identify the optimal carbonization temperature that maximizes the specific capacitance, cyclic stability, and rate capability of the carbon electrodes. In doing so, we aspire to make a substantial contribution to the advancement of high-performance and environmentally friendly supercapacitors.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Methodology: To understand how carbonization temperature affects the electrochemical performance of activated carbon electrodes, we will examine morphological and structural changes using Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy and, Brunauer-Emmette-Teller (BET) Analysis [ [ 8 ]]. We will then employ comprehensive electrochemical analysis techniques including cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge/discharge (GCD) measurements, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) [ [ 9 , 10 ]]. These analyses will allow us to evaluate specific capacitance (ability to store charge per unit area), energy density (amount of energy stored per unit weight), power density (rate at which energy can be delivered), and cycling stability (ability to maintain performance over repeated charge/discharge cycles) of the electrodes. By investigating these factors, we aim to shed light on the underlying mechanisms responsible for the observed variations in electrochemical performance.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Hybrid-Composite Electrodes: Furthermore, in the realm of supercapacitor performance enhancement, researchers are actively exploring the combination of activated carbons (ACs) with transition metal oxide to create hybrid-composites (HC) [ [ 11 ]]. This strategy leverages the synergistic effects of electric double-layer capacitors (EDLC) and pseudocapacitors.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Among the transition metal oxides, manganese dioxide (MnO 2 ) has emerged as a popular choice for supercapacitor applications due to its affordability, natural abundance, strong redox properties, and non-toxic nature [ [ 12 ]]. However, MnO 2, suffers from poor conductivity, necessitating its combination with carbonaceous materials to improve electrical conductivity.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In summary, this research aims to provide valuable insights into the optimal carbonization temperature for specific biomass sources, determining the most favorable conditions, particularly, the carbonization temperature, for producing high electrochemical performance activated carbon-electrodes (AC-electrodes). Furthermore, it also involves a comparison between these AC-electrodes with their hybrid-composite counterparts (HC-electrodes) to assess their suitability in supercapacitor applications.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: By addressing this knowledge gap, our goal is to make significant contributions to the development of efficient and sustainable energy storage devices [ [ 15 ]]. This effort aligns with the urgent need to meet the growing demand for clean energy solutions while minimizing environmental impact [ [ 16 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: For this investigation, wood waste was gathered from local joineries in Kathmandu, Nepal. The analytical-grade activating agent used to prepare the activated carbons was 85 % H 3 PO 4 with a specific gravity of 1.73 g/ml (15.0 M), which was provided by Fischer Scientific, India (P) Ltd. Various chemical reagents (carbon black, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), N-methyl pyrrolidine (NMP), and MnO 2 were from Sigma-Aldrich (USA) and APS Ajax Finechem (Australia). The Ni-foam substrate used in the experiments was obtained from PRED MATERIALS International (USA).

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Sundried wood waste was finely ground and sieved (150 μm mesh size). 80 g of powder was mixed with an equal volume of 85 % H 3 PO 4 and wetted at 25 °C for 24 h. This 1:1 ratio, previously determined to yield optimal results, was chosen based on our prior research [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] ]]. The mixture was then heated to 110 °C for 2 h, following established synthesis procedures [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The prepared sample was divided into four 20 g portions, carbonized individually in separate steel boats at 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C, and 700 °C for 3 h each under a continuous 100 mL/min flow N 2 in a tube furnace. Omitting a 300 °C carbonization followed recommendations in the literature suggesting its ineffectiveness for AC production [ [ 20 ]]. During carbonization, the absence of oxygen facilitated volatile component removal and carbonization. The primary objective was to identify the optimal carbonization temperature for ACs suitable for supercapacitor electrodes.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Each resulting sample was air-cooled and washed with hot distilled water until neutral pH. After complete drying, the samples were finely powdered again, resulting in four distinct ACs: AC-400 °C, AC-500 °C, AC-600 °C, and AC-700 °C. These ACs were subsequently employed for further structural and electrochemical characterization [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] ]].

segments.text: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) of raw wood powder was performed using a SDT Q600 Version 20.9, Build 20 thermogravimetric analyzer (USA).

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: 1 mg of carbon black powder

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Maintaining an 8:1:1 ratio (AC:carbon black:PVDF), this mixture was dispersed in 200 mL of N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) solution to form a uniform electrode slurry. The slurry was then applied onto a 1 cm 2 area of four separate rectangular Ni-foam electrode substrates. After drying overnight in a 70 °C oven, these standardized electrodes were ready for electrochemical testing.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Additionally, hybrid composite electrodes (HCEs) were prepared following the same procedure, but with a 1:1 ratio of AC to manganese dioxide (MnO 2 ), as suggested by previous research [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] , 21 ]]. Similar to the standard electrodes, these HCEs were dried overnight in a 70 °C oven.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Before further testing, all electrodes, both standard and hybrid-composite, were immersed in a 6 M KOH aqueous electrolyte solution overnight. This crucial step aimed to remove any contaminants and activate the electrode surfaces, ensuring reliable and accurate electrochemical performance [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] , 21 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The performances of the four as-fabricated electrodes, hybrid-electrodes (HEs) and MnO 2 electrode were evaluated individually using a three-electrode setup in a 6 M KOH aqueous solution. Pt plates and Ag/AgCl served as counter and reference electrodes, respectively. All experiments were conducted at room temperature using a ‘Metrohm Autolab (PGSTAT 302 N) potentiostat/galvanostat’ system [ [ [17] , [18] , [19] , 21 , 22 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Cyclic voltammetry (CV) analysis provided insights into the redox behavior and charge storage potential of the electrodes. Measurements were conducted within a potential window of −1.0 to −0.2 V at various scan rates (2, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 mV s −1 ) [ [ 23 , 24 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) tests assessed the electrodes' charge/discharge performance at different current densities (1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, and 20 Ag -1 ). Cyclic stability (% retention) was estimated based on data from these tests [ [ 21 , 22 , 25 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data, acquired using a 10 mV perturbation signal across a frequency range of 100 kHz to 0.1 Hz, provided insights into the impedance characteristics of the electrodes and the resistance within the system [ [ [21] , [22] , [23] ]]. The data was analyzed using the Nova 1.11 program.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Fig. 1 shows the TGA curve of raw wood powder from Terminalia elliptica , revealing distinct breakdown stages as discussed below.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Moisture Evaporation: An initial minor weight loss around 100 °C corresponds to the typical moisture removal range for wood.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Hemicellulose Degradation: Between 200 and 400 °C, the weight loss visually depicted in Fig. 1 indicates the degradation of hemicellulose, a key wood component.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Cellulose Decomposition: A noticeable weight loss between 300 and 400 °C signifies the decomposition of cellulose, another major component, in organic volatile substances present in the raw wood powder [ [ 26 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Optimal activation: A substantial weight loss exceeding 60 % at around 400 °C suggests substantial chemical transformations, indicating the optimal activation temperature for AC production from this wood powder. Beyond this point, the weight remains stable, confirming 400 °C as the ideal temperature for AC production from Terminalia elliptica wood powder.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Building on the TGA results, we aimed to validate 400 °C as the ideal carbonization temperature for producing ACs from the H 3 PO 4 -activated raw wood powder. To investigate this, the material was divided into four portions, each carbonized at 400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C, and 700 °C. The resulting ACs (AC-400 °C, AC-500 °C, AC-600 °C, and AC-700 °C) were then comprehensively characterized using various instrumental techniques (XRD, Raman spectroscopy, FTIR spectroscopy, SEM, TEM, and BET analysis).

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Fig. 2 showcases the X-ray diffraction pattern of the activated carbon prepared at different temperatures. Notably, the pattern for AC-400 °C displays a broader hump compared to those for AC-500 °C, AC-600 °C, and AC-700 °C. This observation indicates a higher degree of amorphousness in the carbon structure synthesized at 400 °C.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml

segments.text: XRD of activated carbons prepared for analysis.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The increasing sharpness and narrowing of the peaks with increasing carbonization temperature beyond 400 °C suggest a transition towards more ordered crystalline structures [ [ 19 , 27 ]]. This process known as “graphitization”, aligns carbon atoms into hexagonal layers similar to graphite. While this orderly arrangement reduces the amorphous character, it can also come at the expense of certain desirable properties like surface area and pore volume, which are crucial for some applications of activated carbon [ [ 21 , 28 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In conclusion, the XRD analysis reveals a trade-off between the degree of amorphousness and the level of carbon ordering achieved at different temperatures. While AC-400 °C exhibits a more amorphous structure, potentially offering advantages in terms of surface area and porosity, the higher temperatures promote graphitization and a more organized crystalline structure, which might impact certain functionalities [ [ 29 , 30 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Complementing the insights from XRD, Raman spectroscopy provides valuable information about the vibrational modes of atoms and molecules within the material, revealing details about its bonding and disorder. In Fig. 3 , the Raman spectra of the activated carbons highlight characteristic peaks relevant to carbon structures.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml

segments.text: Raman spectra of activated carbons prepared for analysis.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: A prominent D-band observed in the spectrum of AC-400 °C signifies the presence of disordered sp 2 carbon, frequently encountered in amorphous materials. The intensity of this band reflects the degree of disorder, and notably, the G/D ratio for AC-400 °C is less than 1 (0.97), indicating a relatively high level of defect-rich amorphous character. In contrast, we expect higher-temperature ACs (500, 600, and 700 °C) to exhibit lower amorphosity and a more ordered structure. Consequently, their spectra are likely to show intensified G-bands, corresponding to ordered sp 2 carbon, leading to G/D ratios exceeding 1, as suggested by Fig. 3 . This shift highlights the transition towards a more graphitic structure with increasing carbonization temperature.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: To summarize, the Raman analysis reveals that AC-400 °C possesses a higher degree of disorder and amorphousness, evidenced by its low G/D ratio and dominant D-band. Conversely, the higher-temperature ACs exhibit G/D ratios greater than 1, suggesting a less amorphous and more organized graphitic character due to increased carbon ordering at higher temperatures [ [ 31 ]].

segments.text: Notably, AC-400 °C and AC-500 °C exhibit prominent hydroxyl (OH) groups around 3400 cm −1 , likely due to surface functionalization or adsorbed water molecules. These groups can influence surface chemistry, wettability, and interaction with electrolytes in supercapacitor applications [ [ 32 ]]. In contrast, AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C do not show significant hydroxyl peaks, presumably due to their higher treatment temperatures leading to desorption or decomposition of these functional groups, resulting in a more carbonized structure [ [ 32 ]].

They contribute to increased surface area, improved electrochemical reactivity, and enhanced electrical conductivity, leading to efficient energy storage and delivery [ 35 ].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Notably, AC-400 °C and AC-500 °C exhibit well-defined networks of interconnected pores, ranging in size from micropores to mesopores. This observation suggests that the 400–500 °C temperature range effectively promotes pore development during activation without causing significant pore collapse [ [ 21 , 36 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In contrast, the SEM images of AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C show a less pronounced porous structure. This phenomenon is likely due to the detrimental effects of excessive temperature on pore stability. Higher carbonization temperatures can lead to pore collapse or closure due to structural rearrangements within the carbon framework, ultimately reducing the material's porosity and adsorption capacity [ [ 22 , 36 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Therefore, based on the SEM analysis, temperatures in the range of 400–500 °C seem optimal for achieving the desired porous structure in wood-based ACs. This range effectively balances the creation of new while preserving the integrity of existing ones, making it suitable for the successful production of porous wood-based ACs.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Complementing the SEM analysis, TEM provides a deeper exploration into the fine details of the activated carbons (ACs) porous structures. This is crucial for understanding how carbonization temperature influences the pore characteristics and, consequently, the adsorption capacity of wood-based ACs.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Fig. 6 presents the TEM images of the ACs at x5.0 k (50,000×) magnification, showcasing the intricate networks of pores and their distribution, revealing insights beyond the reach of SEM.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: This TEM analysis confirms that 400 °C offers the most favorable conditions for achieving the desired porous structure. At this temperature, well-defined and accessible pores optimize the material's adsorption potential. Increasing the temperature to 500 °C reveals signs of structural degradation, allowing for effective adsorption. Notably, at 500 °C, the structure shows signs of degradation, with less pronounced pores suggesting a suboptimal morphology for our target application.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Beyond 500 °C, detrimental effects of higher temperature become even more evident. The TEM images indicate a significant reduction in pore volume and potential pore collapse, likely due to the destabilization of the porous network by the intense carbonization process. This further reinforces the conclusion that 400 °C stands out as the most effective temperature for maximizing pore development and achieving the desired porous structure for wood-based activated carbon [ [ 19 , 20 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: AC-400 °C and AC-500 °C display characteristic type II isotherms with minimal nitrogen uptake at low pressures indicating the presence of relatively few micropores. However, a marked increase in nitrogen adsorption around P/P0 = 0.5 accompanied by a hysteresis loop signifies the presence of mesopores (typically 2–50 nm), consistent with findings [ [ 27 , 37 ]]. AC-400 °C exhibits a larger hysteresis loop and continues to adsorb nitrogen until higher pressures, suggesting a more significant mesoporous structure compared to AC-500 °C. This translates to a higher surface area for AC-400 °C (1300 m 2 /g) due to its abundant mesopores offering a larger adsorption surface [ [ 38 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In contrast, AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C lack hysteresis loops, highlighting a dominant presence of micropores or reduced number of mesopores. AC-600 °C possesses a moderate surface area, (280 m 2 /g), while AC-700 °C shows the lowest (67 m 2 /g), indicating a substantial loss of mesopores at higher temperatures [ [ 39 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: These observations highlight the significant influence of carbonization temperature on AC structure. Higher temperatures can close mesopores and promote micropore formation, leading to a reduction in surface area, as suggested by the lack of hysteresis loops at 600 °C and 700 °C. AC-600 °C shows a moderate surface area decrease, while AC-700 °C exhibits the most significant loss, reflecting the collapse or transformation of mesopores into micropores [ [ 20 , 21 , 27 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Structural characterization using XRD, Raman spectroscopy, and FTIR revealed AC-400 °C's optimal porosity and surface area, making it stand out from the others. While AC-500 °C showed similar characteristics, higher temperatures led to reduced performance due to pore loss and structural changes. AC-400 °C's exceptional morphology suggests promising electrochemical potential, particularly in enhancing energy storage for supercapacitors. Therefore, its electrochemical behavior was further investigated through cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge/discharge (GCD), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS).

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The electrochemical performances of the four activated-carbon-electrodes (AC-400 °C, AC-500 °C, AC-600 °C, and AC-700 °C), and four hybrid-composite-electrodes AC:MnO 2 -400 °C, AC:MnO 2 -500 °C, AC:MnO 2 -600 °C, and AC:MnO 2 -700 °C) were measured, compared, and assessed for their findings.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The electrochemical behavior of electrodes at different carbonization temperatures (400 °C, 500 °C, 600 °C, and 700 °C) reveals the following key characteristics:

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: AC electrodes (Fig. 8a) .

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: AC-400 °C electrode (black line ) : shows a large rectangular loop indicative of robust electrical double-layer capacitive (EDLC) behavior with a high specific capacitance [ [ 22 , 23 ]]. Notably, a peak current density of 12 Ag -1 suggests faster ion adsorption/desorption kinetics.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: AC-500 °C (red line): Exhibits a slightly smaller loop area compared to AC-400 °C but retains the rectangular shape, signifying good EDLC behavior.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C (blue and pink lines): Possess narrower loop areas and significantly reduced current densities (2.6 Ag -1 and 1.2 Ag -1 , respectively), implying diminished EDLC performance.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: HC (AC:MnO2) electrodes (Fig. 8b) .

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: HC-400 °C: Displays pronounced redox peaks due to MnO 2 inclusion, showcasing its reversible Mn³⁺/Mn 2 ⁺ conversion reaction [ [ 21 , 22 ]]. Consequently, the current density reaches nearly 20 Ag -1 , highlighting enhanced charge storage due to combined EDLC and pseudocapacitive mechanisms.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: HC-500 °C: Exhibits redox peaks similar to HC-400 °C, while retaining EDLC characteristics observed in the corresponding AC electrode.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: HC-600 °C: While redox peaks are still present, their intensity diminishes compared to HC-400 °C and HC-500 °C. This suggests a decrease in the contribution of pseudocapacitance from MnO 2 due to potential changes in its morphology or surface area at higher carbonization temperatures. The current density also drops, likely reflecting reduced ion accessibility and slower kinetics.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: HC-700 °C: Redox peaks become barely noticeable, indicating minimal pseudocapacitive contribution from MnO 2 at this temperature. The CV curve approaches a rectangular shape similar to AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C, signifying dominance of EDLC behavior. However, the current density remains lower than those observed for the AC electrodes at similar temperatures, suggesting potential detrimental effects of high carbonization on the overall electrode architecture and ion transport within the composite [ [ 21 , 23 , 37 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Carbonization temperature: Lower temperatures (400 °C and 500 °C) promote well-developed porous structures in ACs, leading to higher specific surface areas and enhanced EDLC behavior [ [ 23 , 27 , 37 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Specific Surface Area: The rectangular CV curves and large loop areas of AC-400 °C and AC-500 °C electrodes suggest higher specific surface areas, enabling greater charge storage through electrostatic interactions at the electrode-electrolyte interface [ [ 21 , 24 , 27 , 39 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Truncated Current Densities: AC-600 °C and AC-700 °C electrodes exhibit lower charge storage capacity due to reduced surface areas and possibly decreased pore accessibility, limiting ion access and hindering efficient ion adsorption/desorption [ [ 37 , 38 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Absence of Faradaic Peaks: In all electrodes, the absence of additional peaks beyond the Mn³⁺/Mn 2 ⁺ conversion peaks in HC electrodes confirms the dominance of non-faradaic EDLC behavior during charge/discharge cycles [ [ 19 , 39 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Conclusion: Carbonization temperature significantly impacts the porous structure and specific surface area of ACs, ultimately influencing their electrochemical performance. The CVs primarily suggest EDLC mechanisms, with variations in specific surface area and charge storage capacity across different temperatures. Notably, HC-400 °C demonstrates promising enhanced charge storage through combined EDLC and pseudocapacitive contributions.

segments.text: Examining Fig. 9 a, the GCD curves of AC electrodes exhibit distinct triangular profiles, characteristic of Electric Double-Layer Capacitors (EDLCs) [ [ 21 , 22 ]]. This triangular shape indicates minimal impurities and successful electrolyte ion insertion within the electrode material [ [ 22 , 38 ]]. Notably, the discharge times for AC-400 °C and AC-500 °C were approximately 120 s and 75 s, respectively, yielding specific capacitance values of 183.4 Fg -1 and 137.4 Fg -1 at 1 Ag -1 (calculated using Equation (1) , relating Cs to current density, time duration, loading mass, and potential window). The remaining two ACs’ discharge times and specific capacitances are detailed in Table 1 .

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In contrast, the GCD response of HC electrodes as depicted in Fig. 9 b, a bending nature emerged at a current density of 1 Ag -1 , resembling pseudocapacitive behavior attributed to internal oxidation-reduction reactions in MnO 2 [ [ 27 , 40 ]]. However, the curve exhibited excellent symmetry, indicating remarkable charge-discharge reversibility. The discharge times for AC:MnO 2 -400 °C and AC:MnO 2 -500 °C were approximately 490s and 400s, resulting in specific capacitance values of 491 Fg -1 and 366.3 Fg -1 , respectively [ [ 27 , 39 , 40 ]]. The comparison of discharge times and specific capacitances for AC and hybrid-composite electrodes at different carbonization temperatures can be found in Table 1 .

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Clearly, HCs achieved significantly higher specific capacitances compared to the individual AC electrodes. Among the AC electrodes, AC-400 °C performed the best, while AC:MnO 2 -400 °C excelled among the hybrid composite electrodes. This superior performance can be attributed to synergistic combination of AC and MnO 2 , where non-faradaic (EDLC) and faradaic (redox) mechanisms work effectively together.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: In conclusion, discharge time and specific capacitance trends were influenced by factors, such as synthesis temperature, porosity, impurities, wetting characteristics, and ion diffusion kinetics. These factors shaped the electrochemical behavior of the carbon electrodes. While this study provides valuable insights, further research could explore the long-term cycling stability and scalability of these materials for practical energy storage applications.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Evaluating the long-term performance of supercapacitor electrodes is crucial. Therefore, we assessed the cyclic stability of our electrodes by monitoring their capacity retention (%) over 1000 consecutive charge-discharge cycles at a current density of 3 Ag -1 . Fig. 10 a and b depict the capacity retention results for both activated carbon (AC) and hybrid-composite (AC:MnO 2 ) electrodes.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: For ideal supercapacitors, maintaining a high and stable capacitance over extended cycles is essential. Interestingly, all electrodes exhibited an initial stabilization phase, where capacitance remained relatively constant until approximately 200 cycles. However, beyond 200 cycles, a gradual decline in specific capacitance was observed for all samples. Notably, the decrease after 1000 cycles varied significantly across the AC electrodes: 4 % for AC-400 °C, 9.7 % for AC-500 °C, 23.6 % for AC-600 °C, and 40.8 % for AC-700 °C. This capacity loss is often attributed to the gradual decomposition of electroactive materials into the electrolyte during repeated charging and discharging. Over time, these cycles can lead to material breakdown and dissolution, ultimately reducing overall capacitance [ [ 41 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The hybrid-composite-electrodes (AC:MnO 2 -electrodes) presented a remarkably consistent trend in cyclic stability. In particular, the AC:MnO 2 -400 °C electrode showcased exceptional performance, retaining 99.4 % of its initial capacitance after 1000 cycles. This outstanding stability can be attributed to the presence of MnO 2 in the composite. MnO 2 's intrinsic pseudocapacitive behavior and redox reactions likely play a crucial role in mitigating excessive material degradation during cycling, making it a promising candidate for applications demanding long cycle life [ [ 22 , 42 ]]. Interestingly, the AC-400°C-electrode without MnO 2 addition, also demonstrated respectable cyclic stability, maintaining 97.1 % of its initial capacitance. This suggests that both carbonization temperature and material composition influence long-term performance.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Understanding the internal resistance within electrochemical systems is crucial for optimizing performance. To gain insights into this aspect, we conducted EIS measurements on both activated carbon (AC) and hybrid-composite (AC:MnO 2 ) electrodes. These measurements were performed in a 6 M KOH aqueous solution over a frequency range of 100 KHz to 0.1 Hz. The resulting Nyquist plots ( Fig. 11 a and b), provide valuable information about the impedance behavior of these electrodes.

segments.text: Fig. 11 a and 11. b: Nyquist plots of the AC-electrodes and AC:MnO 2 -electrodes at the perturbation signal with 10 mV AC voltage in 6 M KOH aqueous solution at frequencies ranging from 100 KHz to 0.1 Hz. Fig. 11

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: The observed impedance patterns in the Nyquist plots reveal distinct characteristics. At high-frequencies, an incomplete semicircular curve appears, reflecting the presence of polarization resistance. This resistance arises from the transfer of electrolyte ions into the porous electrode material. In contrast, the low-frequency region exhibits a linear curve indicative of capacitive behavior, consistent with previous research [ [ 43 , 44 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Further analysis of these plots reveals a clear trend. The AC-400°C-electrode ( Fig. 11 a ) displays superior conductivity compared to its counterparts (AC-500°C-electrode, AC-600°C-electrode, and AC-700 °C).

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: This superiority is evident in its remarkably lower internal resistance, approximately 0.41Ω, compared to the other AC electrodes. This enhanced performance can be attributed to its higher specific capacitance (as discussed previously), which facilitates efficient movement of ions and electrons within the electrode structure, thereby improving overall conductivity [ [ 45 ]].

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Conversely, the other AC electrodes exhibit higher internal resistances, ranging from 0.48 Ω to 0.73 Ω. These higher resistances are directly related to their comparatively lower specific capacitance.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Similarly, among the HC electrodes ( Fig. 11 b), AC:MnO 2 -400 °C stands out with a significantly lower resistance of 0.36 Ω compared to the AC-400°C-electrode. The lower resistance in AC:MnO 2 -400 °C is again a consequence of its high specific capacitance, leading to better ion transport and, consequently, enhances conductivity.

segments.path: D:\机器学习-超级电容器\三电极端点扩充_20261018\new_sources\PMC10869866\main.xml
segments.text: Therefore, the EIS analysis highlights the advantage of preparing AC electrodes at 400 °C (AC-400°C-electrode) compared to higher carbonization temperatures. The strong correlation between internal resistance and specific capacitance emphasizes their key roles in influencing electrode conductivity. The insights are valuable for further development and optimization of electrochemical systems [ [ 46 ]].

Electrospinning fabrication of ethanol lignin/polyacrylonitrile composite 
carbon fibers for supercapacitor applications
Junhao Dai , Jing Li , Kejia Wang , Jing Li
*
, Xin Tong , Daliang Guo , Huifang Zhao
School of Environmental and Natural Resources, Zhejiang University of Science and Technology, Hangzhou 310023, China
ARTICLE INFO
Keywords:
Lignin
Electrospinning
Carbon fibers
Supercapacitors
Electrochemical performance
ABSTRACT
Supercapacitors, known for their high safety, long cycle life, rapid charging and discharging rates, and high 
power density, are widely used in portable electronic devices, aerospace applications, and new energy electric 
vehicles. However, the high cost and environmental impact of polyacrylonitrile (PAN)-based carbon fibers, the 
most commonly used electrode materials, limit their further development. In this study, low molecular weight 
ethanol lignin was mixed with PAN for the first time, and lignin-based carbon fibers with excellent electro -
chemical properties were prepared using electrospinning technology. The study investigated precursor solutions 
with different lignin-to-PAN ratios to optimize electrochemical performance. The prepared nanofibers and car -
bon fibers were systematically characterized using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), scanning electron mi -
croscopy (SEM), and electrochemical analysis. The results indicate that when the lignin-to-PAN mass ratio is 2:1, 
the resulting carbon fibers exhibit the best electrochemical performance, with a specific capacitance of 173.64 F 
g
 1 
at a current density of 0.5 A g
 1
, significantly higher than that of pure PAN carbon fibers. This research 
provides substantial evidence for the use of biomass-based lignin as a sustainable alternative to PAN in carbon 
fiber production and opens new possibilities for the application of lignin-based carbon fibers in energy storage, 
particularly in supercapacitors.
1. Introduction
Supercapacitors are highly valued for their high safety, long cycle 
life, rapid charging and discharging rates, and substantial power den -
sity, are widely deployed across various fields, including portable elec -
tronic devices, aerospace applications, and the rapidly growing sector of 
new energy electric vehicles [ 1 – 3 ]. A critical advantage of super -
capacitors is their high specific capacitance combined with low cost. The 
electrochemical performance of these devices is predominantly deter -
mined by the composition and structure of their electrode materials 
[ 4 – 7 ]. Carbon nanofibers, owing to their low density and excellent 
conductivity, have emerged as the most widely used electrode materials 
[ 8 , 9 ]. These nanostructured materials can be synthesized using various 
methods, including electrospinning, chemical vapor deposition, self- 
assembly, template-guided synthesis, and hydrothermal trans -
formation [ 10 , 11 ]. Among these, electrospinning stands out as a 
straightforward and controllable method capable of producing high- 
performance nanofibers by adjusting parameters and the composition 
of the spinning precursor solution. Polyacrylonitrile (PAN), with its 
exceptionally high carbon yield, good solubility, appropriate dielectric 
constant, and electrospinning processability, has become the most 
commonly used spinning precursor polymer [ 12 ]. However, PAN ’ s high 
cost, with precursor fibers (PFs) constituting > 50 % of the total cost of 
carbon fibers [ 13 , 14 ], has spurred research into developing lower-cost 
biomass materials as carbon sources mixed with PAN for fiber produc -
tion [ 15 , 16 ]. Lignin, an abundant aromatic polymer in nature with a 
~60 % carbon content, is a promising alternative carbon source for 
preparing carbon fibers.
Owing to its exceptional properties, lignin has attracted considerable 
attention as a promising material for blending with PAN to produce 
high-performance carbon fibers, driving significant advances in this 
field. Xu Lihong [ 17 ] successfully fabricated high-performance nano -
carbon fibers using lignin sulfonate sodium and PAN as precursors 
through electrospinning, pre-oxidation, and carbonization. The result -
ing ACF-4.5 electrode demonstrated a specific capacitance of 286.8 F 
g
 1 
at 1 A g
 1 
and exceptional cycling stability — retaining 97.4 % 
capacitance after 5000 charge-discharge cycles. Similarly, Zhang [ 18 ] 
developed carbon fibers (LP20-CF) by incorporating 20 % lignin into

excellent supercapacitor performance, retaining 94.50 % of their 
capacitance after 1000 cycles. Lai [ 22 ] produced carbon fiber films from

colleagues optimized the lignin-to-PAN ratio in the spinning solution for 
electrospinning, discovering that a 3:7 ratio produced composite fiber 
films with physical and mechanical properties superior to those of 
commercial polypropylene membranes. Despite these advances, utiliz -
ing lignin as a sustainable raw material for carbon fiber production 
necessitates further in-depth research. Key areas include optimizing 
processing parameters, enhancing its compatibility with PAN, and 
comprehensively understanding its impact on the structural and elec -
trochemical properties of the resulting carbon fibers. These efforts are 
essential to fully realizing the potential of lignin as a viable and eco- 
friendly alternative in carbon fiber manufacturing.
Currently, a significant number of studies have been conducted on 
various lignin and PAN (polyacrylonitrile) composites, such as kraft 
lignin and alkaline lignin. However, there is relatively little research on 
ethanol lignin. At the same time, as an organic solvent lignin, ethanol 
lignin has a carbon content of more than 65 %, significantly higher than 
that of other types of lignin, and its cost is lower. Therefore, we con -
ducted research on the ethanol lignin/PAN system. This study intro -
duced low molecular weight ethanol lignin as a carbon source mixed 
with PAN for the first time, producing lignin-based carbon fibers with 
exceptional electrochemical performance. The research investigates the 
optimal lignin-to-PAN ratio in the precursor solution, providing a robust 
foundation for the use of biomass-derived lignin as a sustainable alter -
native to PAN in carbon fiber production.
2. Materials and methods
2.1. Materials
Ethanol Lignin (EL, Mw: 5000; purity: ≥ 90 %) was purchased from 
Jinan Yanghai Environmental Protection Materials Co., Ltd., PAN 
(Mw:100000) was purchased from Macklin Reagent (Shanghai, China). 
N , N -dimethylformamide (DMF, AR), potassium hydroxide (KOH, AR 
purity: ≥ 95 %) were all purchased from Chengdu Kelong Chemical Co., 
Ltd. All reagents were used as received without any further purification.
2.2. Preparation of spinning solution
Using DMF as the solvent, spinning solutions of lignin and PAN with 
a mass fraction of 20 wt% and different mass ratios (1:1, 2:1, 7:3, 3:1, 
4:1, and 0:1 for lignin to PAN) were prepared. The solutions were heated 
at 80

2.3. Preparation of lignin-based nanofibers
As illustrated in Fig. 1 , lignin-based nanofibers were fabricated using 
the electrospinning technique. A 5 mL medical syringe was employed to 
draw the prepared spinning solution, which was then secured onto a 
push pump and connected to a No. 20 needle at the tip. A layer of 
aluminum foil was wrapped around the roller to collect the fibers ejected 
from the needle. The nanofiber films produced by electrospinning from 
solutions with varying ratios were designated as L-50 %, L-67 %, L-70 %, 
L-75 %, L-80 % and L-0 %. The operational parameters, including the 
push speed, receiving distance, electric field voltage, and roller rotation 
speed, are set to 2 mL h
 1
, 10 cm, 10 kV, and 300 r min
 1 
[ 24 – 26 ], 
respectively.
2.4. Preparation of lignin-based carbon fibers
The lignin-based nanofibers were first placed in a vacuum drying 
oven at 80 
◦
C for 12 h to ensure the complete evaporation of the DMF 
solvent. This step was crucial for fixing the shape of the nanofibers, 
preventing deformation or damage during subsequent processing, and 
enhancing their mechanical strength and stability [ 27 – 30 ]. Following 
this, the fibers were transferred to a tubular furnace and placed on a 
quartz boat for pre-oxidation treatment. Pre-oxidation was essential for 
improving the fibers ’ heat resistance, flame retardancy, and conduc -
tivity. Additionally, this process helped mitigate shrinkage during the 
subsequent carbonization step, thereby maintaining the dimensional 
stability of the fibers to a significant extent [ 31 – 33 ].
The pre-oxidation process was conducted at a temperature of 220 
◦
C, 
with a controlled heating rate of 0.2 
◦
C min
 1
, and a holding time of 2 h. 
After pre-oxidation, nitrogen gas was introduced into the tubular 
furnace for 1 – 2 h to purge any remaining air. The carbonization process 
was then initiated, with the temperature set to 800 
◦
C, a heating rate of 
3 
◦
C min
 1
, and a holding time of 1 h. The fibers were subsequently 
cooled to 200 
◦
C at a rate of 5 
◦
C min
 1
. Upon completion of the 
carbonization process, lignin-based carbon fibers were obtained. The 
prepared composite carbon fibers were designated as LC-50 %, LC-67 %, 
LC-70 %, LC-75 %, LC-80 %, and LC-0 % based on their composition 
ratios.

The functional groups and chemical bond changes of lignin were 
analyzed using a Nicolet IS50 Fourier transform infrared spectrometer

The micromorphological characteristics of the dried nanofibers were

3. Results and discussion
3.1. Chemical structures of lignin
The molecular structure of ethanol lignin significantly influences its

exhibits a broad and diffuse peak around 3400 cm

, corresponding to 
the stretching vibration of the -OH group on the aromatic hydrocarbon 
[ 35 – 37 ]. This peak indicates the presence of hydroxyl groups within the 
lignin structure. The peak near 2930 cm

represents the asymmetric 
stretching vibration of C
–
H bonds in methyl, methylene, and methine 
groups. The sample also displays prominent stretching vibration peaks 
in the range of 1000 – 1700 cm

groups. Additionally, the weak peaks observed between 600 and 800

3.2. Microscopic morphology
3.2.1. lignin-based nanofibers
A well-defined morphology of nanofibers is a critical prerequisite for 
achieving optimal carbonization effects. As illustrated in the scanning 
electron microscopy (SEM) images in Fig. 3 , significant variations in the 
micromorphology of nanofiber films are observed, depending on the 
lignin-to-PAN ratio in the electrospinning solutions.
In Fig. 3 (a) and (f), L-50 % and PNFs exhibit thicker fibers with a 
significant number of beads, presenting a rough surface texture. This 
phenomenon is attributed to the relatively large proportion of PAN, 
resulting in a more viscous solution, which leads to the accumulation of 
the solution at the needle tip, hindering the uniform ejection of the so -
lution and the formation of a stable Taylor cone during the electro -
spinning process.
In contrast, Fig. 3 (b) reveals that L-67 % displays a dense and uni -
form fiber morphology at 3000 × magnification. The fibers are well- 
separated without any adhesion, and Fig. 3 (b1) shows their diameters 
are relatively consistent, predominantly ranging between 200 and 500 
nm, with most fibers falling within this size range. This uniformity 
indicates that the solution of L-67 % has an optimal proportion of its 
components, leading to a better liquid viscosity, more uniform and 
smooth ejection of the solution, thereby achieving a more controllable 
fiber formation process.
Conversely, Fig. 3 (c), (d), and (e) demonstrates that solutions with a 
lower proportion of PAN, compared to L-67 %, result in a sparser fiber 
density. The fibers in these samples exhibit pronounced fiber curling, 
breaking, along with the presence of beaded structures. These defects 
are indicative of insufficient solution viscosity, which compromises the 
stability of the electrospinning process and results in irregular fiber 
formation.
3.2.2. Lignin-based carbon fibers
The structural integrity of carbon fibers plays a crucial role in 
determining their wettability in electrolytes, which in turn significantly 
affects their electrochemical performance as electrode materials. The 
nanofiber films before carbonization exhibit a sparse state, leading to 
poor structural stability, and noticeable fractures appear in the fibers 
after carbonization, as shown in Figs. 4 (a), (c), (d), and (e). Among 
these, the fractures in sample (a) are the most pronounced, consistent 
with the microstructure observed in LC-50 %. Furthermore, in samples 
(c), (d), (e), and (f), the fibers exhibit significant bending after the 
carbonization process. This bending can adversely affect the wettability 
of the fibers by the electrolyte, leading to a reduction in the overall 
electrochemical performance of the electrode material. The decreased 
wettability hinders efficient ion diffusion and charge transfer, ultimately 
compromising the material ’ s effectiveness in energy storage applica -
tions. As can be seen from Fig. 4 (b) and (b1), the fibers of LC-67 % 
exhibit a relatively dense distribution, with uniform diameters and no 
signs of fractures or interconnections, This demonstrates that both lignin 
and PAN maintain excellent thermal stability during carbonization, 
effectively preventing fiber melting phenomena, which may contribute 
to its superior electrochemical performance.
3.3. Electrochemical properties
Fig. 5 (a) presents the CV curves of all samples tested in a 6 M KOH 
electrolyte. The curves exhibit an approximately rectangular shape, 
which is characteristic of ideal capacitive behavior. This suggests effi -
cient charge propagation and favorable ion transport in the KOH elec -
trolyte. The rapid current response observed at each voltage reversal 
point [ 38 , 39 ] indicates that the lignin-based carbon fibers possess 
excellent electrochemical properties, including high capacitive perfor -
mance, low equivalent series resistance (ESR), and fast ion diffusion 
within the electrolyte [ 40 – 42 ]. Among the samples, LC-67 % demon -
strates the largest enclosed area in the CV curve, suggesting a higher 
specific capacitance. This result is consistent with the water contact 
angle measurements, which indicate superior wettability, thereby 
facilitating efficient electron transfer within the electrolyte. The galva -
nostatic charge-discharge (GCD) results of the tested electrodes show

good consistency with the cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements. 
Fig. 5 (b) displays the GCD curves of the samples at a current density of 
0.5 A g
 1
. The curves exhibit a symmetrical, isosceles triangular shape, 
indicative of excellent electrochemical reversibility, a key attribute for 
supercapacitor electrode materials. LC-67 % stands out with the longest 
charge-discharge cycle time of 700 s, significantly outperforming other 
samples, such as LC-0 %.
The electronic conductivity of electrode materials significantly in -
fluences their rate capability. To investigate the conductive properties of 
the composite carbon fibers, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy 
(EIS) measurements were performed on the samples. Fig. 5 (c) presents 
the Nyquist plots from EIS measurements. The curves for LC-50 % and 
LC-0 % lack a semicircle in the high-frequency region, suggesting higher 
impedance and relatively lower capacitive performance. However, their 
nearly vertical curves in the low-frequency region indicate good 
capacitive behavior. As a result, these samples achieve specific capaci -
tances comparable to others, with LC-50 % and LC-0 % reaching 106.75 
F g
 1 
and 136.17 F g
 1
, respectively, at a current density of 0.5 A g
 1
. In 
contrast, the curves for LC-67 %, LC-70 %, LC-75 %, and LC-80 % exhibit 
semicircular shapes in the high-frequency region. The diameter of the 
semicircle corresponds to the charge transfer resistance; a larger diam -
eter indicates poorer charge transfer ability and inferior capacitive 
performance. LC-67 %, with the smallest semicircle diameter, demon -
strates superior charge transfer efficiency. The smaller semicircle in -
dicates that this composite carbon fiber exhibits intrinsic 
pseudocapacitive behavior originating from surface functional group- 
induced redox reactions. Its nearly vertical curve in the low-frequency 
region further confirms its excellent capacitive performance. This phe -
nomenon may be attributed to the rapid diffusion of electrolyte ions. 
Fig. 5 (d) summarizes the specific capacitance of all samples at various 
current densities. LC-67 % exhibits the highest specific capacitance, 
reaching 173.64 F g
 1 
at 0.5 A g
 1
. Notably, even at a high current 
density of 2 A g
 1
, LC-67 % maintains a specific capacitance of 123.48 F 
g
 1
, which is comparable to the performance of other samples at 0.5 A 
g
 1
. This highlights the exceptional rate capability and stability of LC- 
67 % as a high-performance electrode material for supercapacitors. The 
electrochemical performance of electrode materials is fundamentally 
determined by their thermal stability characteristics. As demonstrated 
by thermogravimetric analysis, both lignin and polyacrylonitrile (PAN) 
exhibit excellent thermal stability with residual yields exceeding 35 % at 
800 
◦
C, enabling the preservation of favorable microstructural integrity 
during carbonization. This carbonization process significantly enhances 
the electrode performance through three synergistic effects: (1) 
increased density of electrochemically active sites on carbon fiber sur -
faces, (2) expanded specific surface area, and (3) improved electrolyte 
transport through well-developed porous channels. These structural 
advantages collectively contribute to the outstanding electrochemical 
properties of the resulting carbon fiber electrodes.
Fig. 6 (a, b) presents the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves of LC-67 % 
at various voltage windows and the galvanostatic charge-discharge 
(GCD) curves at different current densities, respectively. An increase 
in the scan rate leads to higher current density, consequently enlarging 
the enclosed area of the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curve. The symmetrical 
shapes of both the CV and GCD curves confirm the excellent rate per -
formance and electrochemical reversibility of LC-67 %. Using the GCD 
curves, the specific capacitance at various current densities was calcu -
lated. As shown in Fig. 6 (c), LC-67 % achieves a remarkable specific 
capacitance of 173.64 F g
 1 
at a current density of 0.5 A g
 1
. Further -
more, when compared with the performance of similar lignin-based 
electrode materials reported in existing literature. As summarized in 
Table 1 , our lignin-based carbon fiber electrode shows significantly 
enhanced performance relative to control electrodes fabricated solely 
through blending without any further processing. Even at a high current 
density of 5 A g
 1
, it maintains a specific capacitance of 68.3 F g
 1
, 
which is approximately 40 % of its performance at 0.5 A g
 1
. This 
demonstrates the material ’ s excellent rate capability, making it suitable 
for high-power applications.
Fig. 6 (d) illustrates the cycling stability of LC-67 % over 3000 
charge-discharge cycles. Repeated charge-discharge cycles can cause 
irreversible alterations in the microstructure of carbon fiber surfaces. 
The carbon fibers after 550 charge-discharge cycles ( Fig. 7 (a)) exhibited 
slight fracture but remained essentially intact, enabling the electrode to 
maintain relatively constant capacitive retention. However, the carbon 
fibers after 750 charge-discharge cycles ( Fig. 7 (b)) displays severe fiber 
fracture, structural damage, and pore collapse. Additionally, sediments 
are observed between the fibers, likely due to electrolyte adhesion, 
which clogs pores and impedes electrolyte diffusion. This reduction in 
active sites and ion transport channels within the lignin-based carbon 
fibers has ultimately led to diminished capacitive retention in the 
electrode.
The material retains 76.16 % of its initial specific capacitance after 
cycling, highlighting its superior positive stability as a flexible electrode 
material for supercapacitors. This excellent cycling performance, com -
bined with its high specific capacitance and rate capability, underscores 
the potential of LC-67 % for practical energy storage applications.
4. Conclusion
Lignin-based nanofibers were prepared by electrospinning using 
ethanol lignin and PAN as raw materials, followed by carbonization to 
produce lignin-based carbon fibers. Electrochemical performance tests 
were then conducted. The results demonstrated that when the lignin-to- 
PAN mass ratio was 2:1, the resulting composite fibers and carbon fibers 
exhibited superior surface morphology compared to pure PAN nano -
fibers and carbon fibers. Furthermore, electrochemical tests revealed 
that this composite material displayed optimal capacitive performance, 
achieving a high specific capacitance of 173.64 F g
 1 
at a current density 
of 0.5 A g
 1 
representing a 27.5 % improvement over pure PAN-derived 
carbon fibers (136.17 F g
 1 
under identical testing conditions). This 
study demonstrates lignin ’ s potential as a sustainable precursor to 
replace expensive PAN raw materials for energy storage applications. 
The findings show promising application prospects and may contribute 
to advancing sustainable development in energy storage materials while 
supporting circular economy objectives. Although the research suc -
cessfully developed composite carbon fibers outperforming pure PAN 
carbon fibers, there remains room for performance enhancement. Future 
work will focus on modifying lignin through graft copolymerization to 
introduce functional groups favorable for electrospinning, thereby 
obtaining composite nanofibers with improved morphology and ulti -
mately enhanced electrochemical performance. While demonstrating 
superior electrochemical performance, the composite carbon fibers also 
exhibit significant potential for mechanical reinforcement and biolog -
ical compatibility applications. In subsequent studies, we will system -
atically optimize this flexible electrode system to achieve 
multifunctional excellence, thereby expanding its applicability across 
biomedical and energy storage domains.

High-efficiency binding of lignin with cesium acetate: Constructing porous 
carbon with ultrahigh specific surface area for supercapacitor 
electrode materials
Jingyuan Lai
